newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian defence minister to visit U.S. this month.
newsitem.headline: Russian defence minister to visit U.S. this month.

text.p: Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov will visit Washington from May 12 to 16 for talks with senior U.S. officials, his ministry said on Tuesday.
Rodionov will meet Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, Defence Secretary William Cohen and possibly President Bill Clinton, a ministry spokesman said.
"We cannot rule out the possibility that the minister will meet President Clinton," he told Reuters.
The spokesman gave no further details but North Atlantic Treaty Organisation expansion is likely to be one of the issues on Rodionov's agenda.
Russia is currently locked in difficult negotiations with U.S. officials over NATO's plans to admit several countries from eastern and central Europe.

Moscow remains strongly opposed to expansion of the Western alliance, saying it poses a direct threat to Russia's own security, but is now focusing its efforts on winning security guarantees in a new Russia-NATO charter.
Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov was due to meet NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana later on Tuesday in Luxembourg to try and overcome the last obstacles to a new partnership.
Russian officials hope that the charter will be ready for signing in Paris by President Boris Yeltsin on May 27.
